title: 4.6 Similarity and Transformations

icans: I can perform a similarity transformation.
I can describe a similarity transformation that maps one figure onto another.
I can decide whether two figures are similar.

vocab: a dilation or a ______________ of rigid motions and dilations
figures that can be mapped onto each other by a similarity _________________

blocks.p: Moves that map the small triangle onto the large one: ______________________

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Similarity transformation: a dilation, or a composition of _______________ and dilations.

blocks.stem: Dilate △ABC with A(1, 1), B(2, 3), C(3, 1) by a scale factor of 2 (center the origin), then reflect the image in the x-axis.
Describe a similarity transformation that maps J(−2, 1), K(−1, 2), L(−1, 1) to J′(2, −2), K′(4, 0), L′(4, −2).

notes: Similar figures: two figures are similar if and only if there is a _______________ transformation that maps one onto the other.

blocks.stem:

a.  2 by 4 and 3 by 6

notes: What stays and what changes: angle measures stay the same; side lengths are multiplied by the _______________.

Is a square with side 3 similar to a square with side 5? If so, give the scale factor.
